security_spec.violation_condition: The kernel's IRQ entry path (do_irq / handle_arch_irq) or KVM's interrupt dispatch reads mip/sip/hvip to determine which external interrupt fired, but in Smivt IVT mode the hardware auto-clears the corresponding interrupt-pending bit on vector-trap entry before the handler executes, so software observes a stale (cleared) pending bit and either misses the interrupt source or incorrectly dispatches.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: csrr.*mip|csrr.*sip|csrr.*hvip in IRQ entry/dispatch paths that assume interrupt-pending bits remain set across IVT-mode hardware vectoring
security_spec.summary: Smivt IVT mode now auto-clears interrupt-pending bits on trap entry; kernel/KVM irqs_pending tracking and mip-read-based IRQ dispatch can observe cleared bits and lose or misroute interrupts

findings.finding: Non-AIA IRQ dispatch reads the interrupt cause from regs->cause (originally derived from CSR_CAUSE in entry.S:187), not from sip/mip. CSR_CAUSE identifies the interrupt type that triggered the trap and is not auto-cleared by the hypothesised Smivt vector-trap entry. No sip/mip CSR read exists in the dispatch path.

AIA IRQ dispatch reads CSR_TOPI in a loop to obtain the top pending interrupt IID. CSR_TOPI is an AIA-specific CSR, not part of the sip/mip/hvip pending-bit set that Smivt would auto-clear. Safe irrespective of IVT-mode vectoring.

The assembly trap entry reads CSR_CAUSE (line 187) and stashes it into pt_regs->cause. CSR_CAUSE encodes why the trap was taken (e.g. IRQ_S_EXT for external interrupt) and is NOT one of the pending-bit CSRs (sip/mip/hvip) that Smivt would auto-clear on vector trap entry.
findings.snippet:
csrr s2, CSR_EPC
csrr s3, CSR_TVAL
csrr s4, CSR_CAUSE          /* ← reads cause, not sip/mip */
csrr s5, CSR_SCRATCH
...
REG_S s4, PT_CAUSE(sp)

findings.finding: The IRQ handler wrapper calls handle_arch_irq(regs) — the function pointer set by the INTC driver. No direct sip/mip/hvip CSR read occurs here. The callee resolves interrupt identity from regs->cause (non-AIA) or CSR_TOPI (AIA), both independent of auto-clearing pending bits.

This chained IPI handler writes csr_clear(CSR_IP, IE_SIE) to acknowledge the software interrupt, but does NOT read sip/mip to determine which interrupt fired. The dispatch decision was already made upstream by the INTC based on regs->cause. If Smivt auto-cleared SIP.SSIE on vector entry, this csr_clear would become a harmless no-op (writing 0 to an already-zero bit). No mis-dispatch can result.

Reads CSR_VSIE (line 371) and CSR_HVIP (line 374) strictly for post-guest-exit state synchronization — detecting guest-initiated changes to VSSIP and LCOFIP by comparing hardware values against the in-memory shadow (csr->hvip). These reads are not used to decide which interrupt to dispatch. The guest-exit cause comes from CSR_SCAUSE (line 856 in kvm_riscv_vcpu_enter_exit), which is unaffected by Smivt.

After guest exit, reads CSR_SCAUSE (line 856) to capture the guest trap cause, plus CSR_HTVAL/CSR_HTINST for hypervisor trap info. CSR_SCAUSE encodes the reason the guest exited (e.g., VS-level external interrupt) — it is a cause register, not a pending-bit register subject to Smivt auto-clearing.

PLIC interrupt handler reads the PLIC claim/complete MMIO register in a loop — no sip/mip/hvip CSR read. The PLIC is a memory-mapped peripheral; its claim register directly provides the hwirq. Smivt vector-trap auto-clearing of sip bits is irrelevant here.

CSR_HVICTL definition includes IPRIO/IPRIOM fields (GENMASK(7,0) and BIT(8)) used by KVM for interrupt-prio threshold control, but no CSR_SIPTHRESHOLD/CSR_SIPSTATUS SMAIA-style CSRs exist for Smivt. The kernel has no smivt ISA extension detected, isa_bitmap entry, or Smivt feature enable/disable path. The IVT-mode pending-bit auto-clear behavior is entirely absent from this kernel version (Linux 7.0-rc5).
